# Metaplate v0.1.2

Metaplate 0.1.2 adds first-class support for sites deployed below a domain subpath and makes the verifier practical for builds that produce more than one image size.

> **Upgrade recommendation:** Recommended for GitHub Pages project sites, documentation portals, monorepo-hosted apps, and any build that emits both social cards and square icons.

## Why upgrade

Root-relative image paths are not sufficient when an application is served from `/project` or another deployment prefix. This release carries `basePath` through framework-neutral, Next.js, and standalone metadata helpers so generated social URLs match the actual host layout.

## Highlights

### Subpath-aware social metadata

- `basePath` composes with routes and image filenames across the public metadata helpers.
- The same plate definition can serve root deployments and repository/application subpaths predictably.
- Next static-export documentation covers `metadataBase`, public PNG output, and deployment prefixes together.

### Mixed-size build verification

- Repeat `--size WIDTHxHEIGHT` groups in one `metaplate verify` invocation.
- A single build check can validate 1200×630 social cards alongside 512×512 icons.
- Default export conditions improve resolution in CommonJS-based TypeScript runners.

## Breaking changes

None. Existing root-deployed URLs and single-size verification commands continue to work.

## Install or upgrade

```sh
npm install metaplate@0.1.2
```

Configure `basePath` only when the deployed application lives below the origin root; root deployments can keep the default.

## Verification

- Route, base-path, and image-path composition is covered across framework-neutral and Next-oriented metadata helpers.
- The CLI verifies multiple size groups in one invocation and retains non-zero failure behavior.
- Package exports resolve through both ESM-oriented and default TypeScript runner conditions.
